title: One sound, other spellings
cando: read a sound that has more than one spelling

about.text: In this lesson you learn the sounds a_e, ay, ea, i_e, igh, o_e, oe, u_e, ue, ew. You hear each sound, you write its letters, and then you read words and a short text with them.
about.speech: In this lesson you learn new ways to write sounds you already know. You hear each sound, you write its letters, and then you read words and a short text with them.
goals: Say the sound for each new spelling
Read a word that has one in it
Write a word that has one in it
Know where in a word each one goes
Read the new words out loud

chapters.title: One Sound, More Than One Spelling: a_e and ay
chapters.text:
This is Lesson 11.
This lesson has no new sounds at all.
Not one. You have them all.
What it has is new ways to WRITE them.
You know the long a. You met it as ai.
Rain. Wait. That is the sound.
Today you meet two more spellings.
The same sound. Written a different way.
The first is ay. Day. Pay. Away.
It comes at the end of a word.
Ai never comes at the end. Ay does.
That is the whole rule for that one.
The second one is stranger. Listen.
The word man. m. a. n. Short a.
Now I add an e at the end.
M. A. N. E. Mane.
The e is not said. It says nothing.
But it reaches back over the n.
And it makes the a say its name.
Man becomes mane. Tap becomes tape.
Cap becomes cape. Hat becomes hate.
We write this a_e. A, gap, e.
The gap is where one letter goes.
Name. n. a_e. m. Three sounds.
Not four. The e is silent.
Late. l. a_e. t. Three sounds.
So now you have three ways to write long a.
Ai in rain. Ay in day. A_e in name.
Which one does a word use?
You cannot hear it. You have to have seen it.
That is not a fault in you. It is English.
Read a lot and you will know.

chapters.title: ea, i_e and igh
chapters.text:
More spellings, no new sounds.
First, long e. You know it as ee.
Feet. Week. That is the sound.
Here is another way to write it. Ea.
Eat. ea. t. Two sounds.
Dream. d. r. ea. m. Four sounds.
Ee and ea are the same sound.
One difference is worth knowing.
Ea can start a word. Eat. Each. Ear.
Ee almost never does.
Now long i. You know it as ie.
Pie. Tie. That is the sound.
Here are two more ways.
The first is i_e. The silent e again.
Pin. Now add an e. Pine.
The e reaches back and makes the i long.
Time. t. i_e. m. Three sounds.
Five. f. i_e. v. Three sounds.
The second is igh. Three letters.
Night. n. igh. t. Three sounds.
Three letters, one sound. That is new.
Light. Right. Might. All the same.
One more thing, and it is useful.
The letter y at the end of a word.
You met y saying its own sound. Yes.
At the END it does something else.
My. Try. Fly. Dry. Why.
It says the long i.
So now long i has four spellings.
Ie in pie. I_e in time. Igh in night. Y in my.
Four ways, one sound. That is English.

chapters.title: o_e, oe, u_e and ew
chapters.text:
Long o and long u.
You know long o. You met it as oa.
Boat. Coat. That is the sound.
Here is another. O_e. The silent e again.
Not. Now add an e. Note.
The e reaches back and makes the o long.
Home. h. o_e. m. Three sounds.
And one more. Oe. Toe. Goes.
There are not many of those. Learn the few.
Now something you have already met.
In Lesson 10 you learned ow. Cow. Now.
But listen to this word. Slow.
Slow. That is not the cow sound.
That is long o.
Ow has two sounds. Cow and slow.
Same as oo in Lesson 9. Boot and foot.
Try one. If it is not a word, try the other.
Now long u. You have it as oo. Boot.
Three more ways to write it.
U_e. June. J. u_e. n. Three sounds.
Ue. Blue. b. l. ue. Three sounds.
Ew. New. n. ew. Two sounds.
Careful with ew. It is not ow.
New is not now. Look at the letters.
So long o has four spellings.
Oa, o_e, ow and oe.
And long u has four.
Oo, u_e, ue and ew.
Two sounds, eight spellings.

reader.title: The New Job
reader.text:
I got a job today.
The man said his name.
I must not be late.
So I take the bus at six.
They pay me at the end of the week.
It is not a lot of pay.
But it is a job. I can make it.

canDo: I can say the sounds a_e, ay, ea, i_e, igh, o_e.
I can read words like name and late.
I can write a word from its sounds.
I can read a short text out loud.
